record.original_question: Does there exist an extremal positive ddc-closed current T directed by a foliation F for which one can estimate the speed at which the Nevanlinna currents τ_r^a converge to T in Theorem 2.1 when tested against smooth observables θ?

evidence.quote: More precisely, for any smooth test form θ of bi-degree (1, 1) on Pk, we have ⟨τar, θ⟩ → ⟨T, θ⟩ as r → 1.
Problem 2.2. (ii) Is there a positive ddc-closed current T, directed by F, extremal, for which one can estimate the speed of the convergence in Theorem 2.1 for smooth observables θ ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a holomorphic foliation by Riemann surfaces on the complex projective space $\mathbb{P}^k$ (with isolated singularities, all hyperbolic). For a leaf $L$ of $\mathcal{F}$ with universal covering $\phi_a:\mathbb{D}\to L$ centered at a point $a$, and for $0<r<1$, let
$$\tau_r^a := \frac{1}{T(r)}\,(\phi_a)_*\!\left(\log^+\!\frac{r}{|\zeta|}\,[\mathbb{D}_r]\right)$$
be the associated Nevanlinna current of bi-degree $(1,1)$ on $\mathbb{P}^k$, where $T(r)$ is the Nevanlinna characteristic that normalizes the mass. It is known that, generically, $\tau_r^a$ converges weakly as $r\to 1^-$ to a positive $dd^c$-closed current $T$ directed by $\mathcal{F}$, i.e. for every smooth test $(1,1)$-form $\theta$ on $\mathbb{P}^k$,
$$\langle \tau_r^a,\theta\rangle \longrightarrow \langle T,\theta\rangle.$$

Question: Does there exist a foliation $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathbb{P}^k$ and an extremal positive $dd^c$-closed current $T$ directed by $\mathcal{F}$ for which one can give a quantitative estimate (a rate, as a function of $r\to 1^-$) on the speed of convergence
$$\big|\langle \tau_r^a,\theta\rangle - \langle T,\theta\rangle\big|$$
when tested against smooth $(1,1)$-forms $\theta$?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return a paper that explicitly establishes a quantitative rate of convergence for Nevanlinna currents toward an extremal $dd^c$-closed directed current on $\mathbb{P}^k$. Related work addresses existence and structure of Nevanlinna/Ahlfors currents and foliation cycles, but no concrete rate-of-convergence result was located. The status is therefore inconclusive from available sources.

status_evidence.title: Entire Curves Producing Distinct Nevanlinna Currents
status_evidence.snippet: Studies multiplicity of Nevanlinna currents produced by entire curves but does not address speed of convergence.
status_evidence.claim: Related work focuses on existence/distinctness of Nevanlinna currents, not quantitative convergence rates.

status_evidence.title: Entire curves generating all shapes of Nevanlinna currents
status_evidence.snippet: Concerns the variety of Nevanlinna currents arising from holomorphic disks, without quantitative speed estimates.
status_evidence.claim: No explicit rate of convergence in the foliated $\mathbb{P}^k$ setting is provided.
